L01.note: 14 is the hub: -7 is its negative half and 18 is 14+4, so it reads as the value the others were derived from.

L02.note: 7/2 sits at the centre of the family: 2/7 is its reciprocal and 7/3 shares its numerator.

L03.note: 3 = 5 + (-2), the sum of the two other plausible roots, with -7 a sign-slip of the same pair.

L04.note: 14.5 is the lone non-integer among three round values.

L06.note: 216 is the only clean cube and 72 is exactly 216/3.

L07.note: 6 links to every other value (24 = 4x6, -2 = -6/3, 5 = 6-1); the others link only to it.

L08.note: 5, 9, 17 are all 2^k+1 and -1 is the outlier, but nothing says which side the key is on.

L09.note: -9/2 is the hub: -9 is its double and -5/2 is it plus 2.

L10.note: all four are multiples of 6 and 30 is the central one the others sit +36/-12/-72 from.

L11.note: the set is 14/3, 15/3, 16/3, 17/3 and only the key is written as the integer 5.

L12.note: 4/6/8 is an even ladder with 1 the outlier; no way to choose inside the ladder.

L13.note: 56.25 is the lone non-integer and a clean square (7.5^2), the shape of a maximum-value answer.

L15.note: 6/5 is the reciprocal of 5/6 and one fifth of 6, so it touches both other real values.

L16.note: 31.75 / 36.75 / 41.75 is a +-5 ladder centred on 36.75, with 17.25 the outlier.

L18.note: 60/70/80 is a ten-ladder and 80 is the value 100 and 60 bracket.

L19.note: 8 is both the sum of 3 and 5 and the partner of the -8 sign-slip.

L20.note: 49 is the hub: 7 is its root, 14 is 2x7, 50 is 49+1.

L22.note: -41 is the only large magnitude; -2, -3 and 7 look like inputs rather than an evaluated result.

L23.note: 15 generates the others (60 = 4x15, 17 = 15+2), so it reads as the source value.

L24.note: two tight pairs (27/29 and 41/44) and nothing separating them.

L25.note: 28, 36, 44 is a +-8 ladder centred on 36; 32 is the inserted odd one.

L26.note: all four are sums of two squares, which discriminates nothing.

L28.note: 26/3, 27/3, 28/3 is a consecutive-thirds ladder and only the key is written as the integer 9.

L29.note: 40.75 is the most computed-looking value but the set is too scattered to read.
